Ok apparently you also have to select the log level for LSP trace. Besides the dropdown there is a gear icon. Please select "trace" instead of "info".

Going from too few logs to too many logs :)
Putting this is in a .txt since github doesn't seem to like that much text

[lsp_trace.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22943255/lsp_trace.txt)
Tried to run `localize_path()` on the `rootPath` parameter seen in the trace, couldn't resolve the path, but it could as soon as I upper-cased the drive letter
@PwaDesu Did you try 4.5 & 4.6? (Not 4.5.1; you encountered the issue in it)

> [@PwaDesu](https://github.com/PwaDesu) Did you try 4.5 & 4.6? (Not 4.5.1; you encountered the issue in it)

Yes, it also happens in 4.5 and 4.6 (dev1). I do not have a mean to compile to more recent 4.6 builds.

The thing is, I understand why you are getting the faulty warning. The check for it is wrong and compares paths like strings instead of filesystem objects. What bothers me more, is that you are still getting duplicated script errors, because the checks in there don't just compare path string and uses `DirAccess::is_equivalent` which in theory should work.

Could you check whether `DirAccess::is_equivalent` can handle the different drive letters on your system?

Also providing the output of the following editor script would help in tracking this down:
```gdscript
@tool
extends EditorScript


# Called when the script is executed (using File -> Run in Script Editor).
func _run():
	var server = Engine.get_singleton("GDScriptLanguageProtocol")
	print(server)
	print(server.get_workspace().get_file_path("file:///f%3A/Programming_Projects/lsp-path-matching-mrp"))
```

Also your trace does not actually include any "Class [x] hides a global script class" errors. If you are able to still reproduce the error, please provide a trace of it as well.

Ah, yes, the trace did not show the error because I had not opened the file at that time. This trace does. 

[lsp_trace_2.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23025222/lsp_trace_2.txt)

As for the results of the editor script execution: 
```
<GDScriptLanguageProtocol#1500034180597>
/f:/Programming_Projects/lsp-path-matching-mrp
false
```
The `false` comes from the following lines I added, which I assume are what you were asking:
```
var dir_access = DirAccess.open("res://");
print(dir_access.is_equivalent("f:\\Programming_Projects\\lsp-path-matching-mrp", "F:\\Programming_Projects\\lsp-path-matching-mrp"));
```

Although it kinda looks like I misunderstood you and did it wrong, because it returns `false` even if I make the drive letters match case?

It's supposed to return `true` for identical paths. So we seem to have two issues here:
1. the checks for the warning message use direct path comparison instead of `DirAccess::is_equivalent`
2. `DirAccess::is_equivalent` doesn't behave correctly in your setup.

I can piece together a fix for 1., but I'm not knowledgeable on 2. someone else will have to dig into that.

There has to be something I'm doing wrong, this is the stable 4.5.1 release so no shenanigans going on there, but I can't get `DirAccess::is_equivalent` to resolve to `true` on seemingly any path

Correction: Comparing `user://` to `user://` and `res://` to `res://` does resolve to `true`, but `F:\\Programming_Projects\\lsp-path-matching-mrp` to `F:\\Programming_Projects\\lsp-path-matching-mrp` doesn't

Alright so I've done a few more tests, I was putting that thought aside because it seemed unlikely, but at this point this hypothesis needed to be tested; On my machine, using `DirAccess::is_equivalent` with the following parameters:
`C:\\` & `C:\\`: `true`
`D:\\` & `D:\\`: `true`
`E:\\` & `E:\\`: `false`
`F:\\` & `F:\\`: `false`
`G:\\` & `G:\\`: `false`

Thus, this appears to be an issue with the drive type. I'm not very knowledgeable in this domain, but  my `C:` and `D:` drives are internal (an SSD and an HDD respectively). My `E:`, `F:` and `G:` drives however are external SSDs connected via USB through an USB hub. 
I'm not sure how this difference matters, but it seemingly does. 
Moving the MRP to my `C:` drive solves the issue.
I can confirm I am also seeing the same error. My project is also on an external SSD rather than the computer's hard drive on Windows

Could you check whether https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/120087 fixes the `DirAccess::is_equivalent` issue? [You can download the CI artifact for testing.](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/testing.html#downloading-a-compiled-build)

> Could you check whether [#120087](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/120087) fixes the `DirAccess::is_equivalent` issue? [You can download the CI artifact for testing.](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/testing.html#downloading-a-compiled-build)

Hello, my apologies for not keeping up with the issue myself (a game development sinkhole opened under me). I appreciate you remembering and attempting to resolve this issue! I haven't even had time to upgrade to Godot 4.6 yet, but I downloaded it just now (where did the cute blue-themed UI go :( ) and will post the results: 

For reproducibility, here's the script I'm using:

```gd
@tool
extends EditorScript


# Called when the script is executed (using File -> Run in Script Editor).
func _run():
	var server = Engine.get_singleton("GDScriptLanguageProtocol")
	print(server);
	print("server#get_workspace()#get_file_path(path_to_current_project_on_external_drive): ", server.get_workspace().get_file_path("file:///f%3A/Programming_Projects/lsp-path-matching-mrp"));
	var dir_access = DirAccess.open("user://");
	print("DirAccess#is_equivalent(C drive) (internal SSD): ", dir_access.is_equivalent("C:\\", "C:\\"));
	print("DirAccess#is_equivalent(D drive) (internal HDD): ", dir_access.is_equivalent("D:\\", "D:\\"));
	print("DirAccess#is_equivalent(E drive) (external SSD): ", dir_access.is_equivalent("E:\\", "E:\\"));
	print("DirAccess#is_equivalent(F drive) (external SSD): ", dir_access.is_equivalent("F:\\", "F:\\"));
	print("DirAccess#is_equivalent(G drive) (external SSD): ", dir_access.is_equivalent("G:\\", "G:\\"));
```
